title: File:Miniature Locomotive at the Hesston Steam Engine Museum - July 2010.jpg
desc: The 1/4 sized railway was originally developed to be used for transportation in World's Fairs, Expositions that encompassed hundreds of acres and transported people around these large areas but also in the small amusement parks and roadside attractions. These type of trains date back to the 1890s the oldest the museum has is over 100 years old built in 1922.

title: File:Whitcomb Locomotive at the Hesston Steam Engine Museum - December 2010.jpg
desc: Whitcomb Locomotive Works was founded in 1878 and closed in 1952. It specialized in rail cars for material handling, such as coal mining or steel production. This engine is part of a small rail car that appeared to be used to simply move single cars around in a railyard. Seen in the Hesston Steam Engine Museum, in Hesston, Indiana.
